before.domestic_norm: Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Salud
before.assessment_summary: Art. 35 frac. XIX of the SS Interior Regulation explicitly designates the DGE as the RSI National Focal Point and assigns IHR Article 4 duties. Actor fit is strong. Procedure fit is partial: 24-hour availability, internal contact lists, and WHO communication protocols are not codified. Coordination with SRE (DGRI) and COFEPRIS is implied but not operationally specified.

after.domestic_norm: Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Salud
after.assessment_summary: The DGE focal-point role is identified. Its full procedure and coordination assessment must also consider NOM-017 sections 6.6.3, 6.6.4 and 8.1.4. The referenced manual and operational arrangements are not evaluated here.
after.reviewer_notes: Documentary correction from audit 2026-10-14. Not an independent expert validation; legal sufficiency remains to be reviewed.

before.domestic_norm: NOM-017-SSA2-2012, Para la vigilancia epidemiológica
before.assessment_summary: NOM-017 numeral 6.6.1-6.6.2 reiterates and operationalises the DGE NFP designation at the technical-normative level, confirming DGE as the domestic focal point for PHEIC notifications. Provides operational specificity not found in the Reglamento Interior, but does not fully specify 24-hour communication protocols or backup NFP contacts.

after.domestic_norm: NOM-017-SSA2-2012, Para la vigilancia epidemiológica

before.domestic_norm: Ley General de Salud
before.assessment_summary: Art. 134 establishes the SINAVE and assigns SS the mandate to develop epidemiological surveillance capacity at all levels. Fourteen fracciones cover detection, notification, laboratory confirmation, and information management. Does not explicitly reference IHR Annex 1 benchmarks or time-bound development milestones.

after.domestic_norm: Ley General de Salud
after.assessment_summary: LGS Article 133, section II assigns the Ministry of Health responsibility for establishing and operating SINAVE under the Law and implementing provisions. The full scope of IHR Article 5 also requires review of the technical standard and its referenced documents.
after.reviewer_notes: Documentary correction from audit 2026-10-14. Not an independent expert validation; legal sufficiency remains to be reviewed.

before.domestic_norm: Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Salud

after.domestic_norm: Reglamento Interior de la Secretaría de Salud
after.assessment_summary: Art. 35 frac. X assigns DGE operational responsibility for SINAVE, providing the institutional anchor for national surveillance system development. before.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
before.assessment_summary: Art. 14 of the RLGS Sanidad Internacional explicitly assigns the duty to notify WHO of events meeting IHR notification criteria, referencing international obligations. This is the most direct regulatory anchor for the Art. 6(1) notification obligation. Procedure for Annex 2 risk assessment is not domestically specified.
before.reviewer_notes: Closest domestic anchor to IHR Art. 6 notification duty.

before.domestic_norm: Ley General de Salud
before.assessment_summary: Art. 134 SINAVE mandate covers detection and notification at all levels including primary care and community levels (fracs. IV, V, VI). This provides partial anchoring for Annex 1A par.4 community-level detection capacities. No provision specifies the minimum capacity benchmarks from IHR Annex 1A par.4.

after.domestic_norm: Ley General de Salud

before.domestic_norm: Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos
before.assessment_summary: Art. 14 CPEUM guarantees due process and prohibits deprivation of rights without fair legal process, providing the constitutional constraint on compulsory health measures under IHR Art. 23(3). Rights safeguard fit is strong at the constitutional level, but specific procedural guarantees for travellers subject to health measures are not operationalised in implementing legislation.

after.domestic_norm: Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos
after.assessment_summary: Art. 14 CPEUM guarantees due process and prohibits deprivation of rights without fair legal process, providing the constitutional constraint on compulsory health measures under IHR Art. 23(3). Rights safeguard fit is strong at the constitutional level, but specific procedural guarantees for travellers subject to health measures are not operationalised in implementing legislation.
after.reviewer_notes: Audit 2026-10-14: this is a provisional record-level safeguard flag, not proof that safeguards are absent from Mexican law or newly required only in 2024. Review the wider framework and instrument versions.

before.domestic_norm: Ley General de Salud

Does not address the specific Art. 23(3) requirement that no health measure be applied without the traveller's informed assent and adequate information.

before.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
before.assessment_summary: Art. 9 RLGS lists required maritime health documentation and governs its use at designated ports, partially anchoring the Art. 37 Maritime Declaration of Health obligation. Specific form, content requirements, and submission timing for the Maritime Declaration are not specified in the domestic corpus.

after.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
after.assessment_summary: Article 31 requires the ship captain to submit the maritime declaration of health on arrival in national territory in the form established by the IHR; the captain and any ship doctor must provide information requested by the health authority.
after.reviewer_notes: Documentary correction from audit 2026-10-14. Not an independent expert validation; legal sufficiency remains to be reviewed.

before.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
before.assessment_summary: Art. 9 RLGS governs aviation health documentation at designated international airports, partially anchoring Art. 38 Aircraft General Declaration requirements. Art. 5 RLGS definition of aeronautical terms provides definitional anchoring. Specific form and completion requirements for the Health Part are not domestically codified.

after.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
after.assessment_summary: Article 30 requires the aircraft commander or chief cabin attendant to present the general declaration on landing at a national airport, including health information in the IHR form, and provide additional information requested by the health authority.
after.reviewer_notes: Documentary correction from audit 2026-10-14. Not an independent expert validation; legal sufficiency remains to be reviewed.

before.assessment_summary: No domestic provision found that specifically prohibits charging travellers for personal health measures (examination, vaccination, prophylaxis, health documents) required under IHR Art. 40. The corpus does not contain a traveller health measures fee framework.
before.reviewer_notes: Full gap. No domestic Art. 40 implementation found.

after.domestic_norm: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
after.assessment_summary: Article 7 of the International Health Regulation establishes free international health services and documents, with exceptions for specified services and other applicable provisions. These exceptions and scope must be compared with IHR Article 40; no full-compliance conclusion follows.
after.reviewer_notes: Documentary correction from audit 2026-10-14. Not an independent expert validation; legal sufficiency remains to be reviewed.

before.domestic_article: Art. 56, párrafo 4 (regulaciones y restricciones no arancelarias / sanidad)
before.assessment_summary: Art. 56 para. 4 Ley Aduanera references health-based non-tariff restrictions on goods and cargo, providing a contextual anchor for the regulatory framework within which health charges on goods might be assessed. No domestic provision establishes a published schedule of charges for health measures applied to goods, cargo, or containers as required by IHR Art. 41.
